question: How does the pepM pre-screen behave on a second clade, and where do its false positives come from?
why: To see whether the screen behaves the same outside Enterobacterales, where all prior validation was done, and to characterise its false positives.
dataset: 323 actinomycete genomes spanning three documented phosphonate lineages: Saccharothrix 62 (phosphonothrixin), Glycomyces 55 (phosphonoglycans), S. hygroscopicus 39 (bialaphos), S. griseus 167.
method: Ground truth from an unscreened arm - every genome through antiSMASH - against the screen's per-genome verdicts from the screened arm. Same code, same genomes, params in JSON files.
reading: Sensitivity holds: 31/31, or 30/30 excluding the self-match, with 37 points of headroom between the cut at 100 and the weakest true positive at 137. What does not hold is the false-positive rate (7.9% against 0.32% on Erwiniaceae) and the clean score gap. Only ONE true positive falls inside the negative range: 30 of 31 sit above the top negative of 157, and the second-weakest true positive is 164. A cut at 160 would give 30/31 with zero false positives; the current cut at 100 buys the last genome for 23 false positives.

cost.note: antiSMASH fell 7.3x here at 9.6% BGC-positive, against 1.7x on P. ananatis at 56%.

CORRECTION: An earlier version of this file, and of the white paper, called this a HELD-OUT clade. That is wrong. Six of the seven curated pepM references are actinomycete (S. rubellomurinus, S. luridus, S. fradiae, Glycomyces sp. NRRL B-16210, Streptomyces sp. NRRL B-2790, S. durhamensis); only HvrA is Pantoea. Glycomyces sp. NRRL B-16210 is IN this test set and scores 828 because its own pepM is a reference - a self-match. Actinomycetes are the clade the reference set mostly comes from; Erwiniaceae, with one reference of seven, was the cross-clade test. Sensitivity excluding the self-match is 30/30.

false_positive_diagnosis.what_they_are: Full-length homologues at 31.9-37.7% identity with ~99% coverage - the isocitrate lyase / PEP mutase superfamily (Pfam clan CL0036), which actinomycete genomes carry in quantity. Not fragments, not noise: the S. griseus false positives repeat the same 33.5% identity and 99% coverage, one conserved paralog family across a species.
false_positive_diagnosis.why_more_references_do_not_help: Adding the four characterised actinomycete pepMs from the reference BGCs (argolaphos, bialaphos, phosphinothricin, phosphonothrixin) lifted the weakest true positive from 137 to 147 - still below the top negative at 157 - and ADDED one false positive. The big gains were self-matches: Saccharothrix sp. ST-888 rose 381 -> 535 because the phosphonothrixin reference BGC is that strain. Best cut keeping 31/31 stayed at 134 with 12 false positives either way.
false_positive_diagnosis.neither_identity_nor_coverage_separates: true positives span 31.1-97.4% identity, false positives 31.9-37.7%; coverage is ~95-100% for both. The weakest true positive (S. hygroscopicus NBRC 3401, 31.1%, 93% coverage) is indistinguishable from the paralogs on every pairwise axis measured.
false_positive_diagnosis.implication: The discriminator is wrong, not the reference set. Pairwise similarity to seven sequences cannot separate a family member from a superfamily paralog at ~33% identity. A profile HMM for the family (PF13714 at its gathering threshold, which is what antiSMASH itself uses) is the candidate fix.
